title: Reading literary prose
summary: Reading fiction the way a writer builds it: imperfect for the scene and preterite for the event, the historic present and the narrative imperfect, free indirect style, epithets, hyperbaton and literary words.
focus: Reading the tense choices, voice and style of literary Spanish prose
content:
## Scene and event: imperfect, preterite, historic present

> Llovía sobre Valdelosa desde el amanecer. Las persianas de la calle Mayor estaban bajadas, el bar olía a café quemado y nadie hablaba. A las once en punto se abrió la puerta y entró una mujer con un abrigo verde. Pidió un vaso de agua, dejó una llave sobre la barra y se fue sin mirar atrás.

The **imperfect** paints the backdrop: **llovía**, **estaban**, **olía**, **hablaba**. The **preterite** moves the plot, one event after another: **se abrió**, **entró**, **pidió**, **dejó**, **se fue**.

Retold in the **presente histórico**, the scene comes closer, as if it were happening now: **A las once en punto se abre la puerta y entra una mujer.**

## The narrative imperfect

> El tren de Valdelosa salía a las seis. Aquella mañana, Tomás llegó a la estación con diez minutos de margen. Un año después, la línea cerraba para siempre.

The first **salía** is an ordinary imperfect: the timetable, a habit. The last **cerraba** is different: one finished event, told as if in slow motion. This **imperfecto narrativo** (also called **imperfecto de ruptura**) is common in novels and the press, as in **Dos días después, el alcalde dimitía.** It gives an ending weight and solemnity, while the preterite **cerró** would only report it.

## Free indirect style

> Elvira guardó la carta en el cajón. ¿Y si su hermano tenía razón? No, imposible. Mañana iría al notario, firmaría los papeles y aquella casa dejaría de ser un problema. Cerró el cajón con llave.

No **pensó que** introduces it, yet the middle sentences are Elvira's thoughts. In **estilo indirecto libre** the narrator keeps the third person and moves the tenses back (**tenía**, **iría**, **firmaría**), but the questions, exclamations and words (**No, imposible**) are the character's own. Ask who would say each sentence. If the answer is the character, you are inside her head.

## Epithets, hyperbaton and literary words

- An **epíteto** is an adjective placed before the noun to stress a quality it already has: **la blanca nieve**, **el frío mármol**, **las oscuras aguas del pozo**. It adds tone, not information. Some adjectives change meaning: **un viejo amigo** (a long-standing friend) vs **un amigo viejo** (an elderly friend).
- **Hyperbaton** in prose fronts a complement for rhythm: **De la casa de su infancia, nada quedaba en pie.**
- Literary vocabulary: **el umbral** (threshold), **la penumbra** (half-light), **el crepúsculo** (twilight), **el anhelo** (longing), **efímero** (fleeting), **inefable** (beyond words), **susurrar** (to whisper), **yacer** (to lie, often of the dead), **vislumbrar** (to glimpse).

vocabulary.example: Se quedó un momento en el umbral, sin decidirse a entrar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She stood for a moment in the doorway, unable to decide whether to go in.

vocabulary.example: La biblioteca estaba en penumbra cuando sonó el teléfono.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The library was in half-light when the phone rang.

vocabulary.example: Volvieron al pueblo con el último crepúsculo de agosto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They returned to the village in the last twilight of August.

vocabulary.example: Su único anhelo era ver otra vez el mar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: His only longing was to see the sea once more.

vocabulary.example: La fama del pintor fue tan efímera como su juventud.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The painter's fame was as fleeting as his youth.

vocabulary.example: Sintió una calma inefable al llegar a la cima.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She felt a calm beyond words when she reached the summit.

vocabulary.example: Le susurró el nombre al oído y se marchó.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She whispered the name in his ear and left.

vocabulary.meaning: to lie (literary; often of the dead)
vocabulary.example: En aquella colina yacen los fundadores del pueblo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The founders of the village lie on that hill.

vocabulary.example: Tras la curva vislumbraron por fin las luces del valle.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Beyond the bend they at last made out the lights of the valley.

vocabulary.meaning: epithet: an adjective before the noun that stresses a known quality
vocabulary.example: En la blanca nieve, blanca es un epíteto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In la blanca nieve, blanca is an epithet.

vocabulary.meaning: free indirect style: a character's thoughts in the narrator's voice
vocabulary.example: El estilo indirecto libre nos deja oír lo que piensa el personaje.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Free indirect style lets us hear what the character is thinking.

vocabulary.meaning: historic present: the present tense used to tell past events
vocabulary.example: El presente histórico acerca la escena al lector.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The historic present brings the scene closer to the reader.

vocabulary.meaning: narrative imperfect: one finished event told in the imperfect
vocabulary.example: La novela termina con un imperfecto narrativo: al día siguiente, el barco zarpaba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The novel ends with a narrative imperfect: the next day, the ship set sail.

quiz.prompt: In the Valdelosa passage, what do llovía, estaban and olía do?
options: They paint the background of the scene.
They move the story on, one event after another.
They report what a character is thinking.
quiz.correct_answer: They paint the background of the scene.
quiz.explanation: The imperfect describes the setting: the rain, the blinds, the smell. Nothing happens until the preterite se abrió.
hints: Does anything happen in those verbs, or is it all setting?

quiz.prompt: Which verb from the Valdelosa passage moves the story forward?
quiz.explanation: Entró is a preterite: a completed event in the sequence of the plot. Olía and hablaba belong to the scene.

quiz.prompt: Retell in the historic present: A las once se abrió la puerta → A las once se ___ la puerta.
quiz.explanation: The historic present tells a past event in the present to bring it closer: se abre la puerta y entra una mujer.
hints: Present tense of abrir, third person.

quiz.prompt: Un año después, la línea cerraba para siempre. This cerraba is…
options: a narrative imperfect: one finished event, told slowly and solemnly
a habit: the line closed every day
quiz.correct_answer: a narrative imperfect: one finished event, told slowly and solemnly
quiz.explanation: The line closed once, for good. Using the imperfect for a single finished event slows it down and gives it weight: the narrative imperfect.
hints: How many times did the line close for good?

quiz.prompt: In the Elvira passage, whose voice is ¿Y si su hermano tenía razón?
options: Elvira's thoughts, told in the narrator's third person
quiz.correct_answer: Elvira's thoughts, told in the narrator's third person
quiz.explanation: No verb of thinking introduces it, but the doubt is Elvira's: that is free indirect style.
hints: Who would ask herself this question?

quiz.prompt: Elvira thinks: Mañana iré al notario. In free indirect style the text says: Mañana ___ al notario.
quiz.explanation: Free indirect style moves the tenses back like reported speech: iré becomes iría, but mañana, her own word, stays.
hints: The future moves back to the conditional.

quiz.prompt: La blanca nieve cubría el valle. What does blanca add before the noun?
options: Tone: it stresses a quality snow already has (an epithet).
Information: it tells this snow apart from snow of other colours.
Nothing: the word order is a mistake.
quiz.correct_answer: Tone: it stresses a quality snow already has (an epithet).
quiz.explanation: Snow is white anyway, so blanca before the noun is an epithet: it adds atmosphere, not information.
hints: Is there any other kind of snow in the scene?

quiz.prompt: The light in a room at dusk, neither bright nor dark: la ___.
quiz.explanation: La penumbra is half-light, a favourite word of literary description.

quiz.prompt: A lo lejos, entre la niebla, ___ las luces del puerto.
quiz.explanation: Vislumbrar is to glimpse something faint or far away: the lights could just be made out through the fog.

quiz.prompt: Se detuvo en el ___ de la puerta, sin atreverse a entrar. (threshold)
quiz.explanation: El umbral is the threshold: the place between outside and in, often a symbol of hesitation in fiction.

listening.text: El crepúsculo teñía de rojo el río.
listening.meaning: The twilight tinged the river red.
listening.note: New word: teñir = to dye, to tinge.

listening.meaning: Someone was whispering in the half-light.

listening.text: La felicidad de aquel verano fue efímera.
listening.meaning: The happiness of that summer was short-lived.

listening.text: Sintió un anhelo inefable de volver a casa.
listening.meaning: He felt an indescribable longing to go home.

listening.text: En el viejo cementerio yacen sus abuelos.
listening.meaning: His grandparents lie in the old cemetery.
listening.note: Yacer: literary, often of the dead.

listening.text: Aquella noche, el último barco abandonaba el puerto para siempre.
listening.meaning: That night, the last boat left the harbour for ever.
listening.note: A narrative imperfect: one event, told slowly.

listening.text: Desde la ventana se vislumbraban las torres de la catedral entre la niebla.
listening.meaning: From the window you could make out the cathedral towers through the fog.
listening.note: New word: la niebla = the fog.

listening.text: Nadie la esperaba ya; aun así, se quedó un momento en el umbral.
listening.meaning: Nobody was waiting for her any more; even so, she stood a moment in the doorway.

guide.tip: Reading a novel, mark each verb as scene (imperfect) or event (preterite): you will see how every page is built.

conversations.title: At the writing workshop
conversations.scenario: Inés, who runs a creative writing workshop, comments on the opening of Rodrigo's short story.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Rodrigo, tu relato empieza bien: llovía, el bar olía a café, nadie hablaba.
lines.meaning: Rodrigo, your story starts well: it was raining, the bar smelt of coffee, nobody was talking.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Quería que el lector entrara en la escena antes de que pasara nada.
lines.meaning: I wanted the reader to step into the scene before anything happened.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Lo consigues. Pero luego todo sigue en imperfecto y la historia no avanza.
lines.meaning: You manage it. But then everything stays in the imperfect and the story doesn't move.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Pongo en pretérito la llegada de la mujer?
lines.meaning: Shall I put the woman's arrival in the preterite?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí: entró, pidió, se fue. El imperfecto pinta; el pretérito cuenta.
lines.meaning: Yes: she came in, ordered, left. The imperfect paints; the preterite tells.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y el final? Escribí: un año después, el bar cerraba para siempre.
lines.meaning: And the ending? I wrote: a year later, the bar closed for good.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ese imperfecto narrativo funciona: le da un aire solemne, casi de crónica.
lines.meaning: That narrative imperfect works: it gives it a solemn air, almost like a chronicle.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: En la página dos el camarero se pregunta si ella volverá. ¿Se entiende sin poner pensó?
lines.meaning: On page two the waiter wonders whether she'll come back. Is it clear without writing he thought?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, es estilo indirecto libre. Oímos su voz sin que el narrador nos avise.
lines.meaning: Yes, it's free indirect style. We hear his voice without the narrator telling us.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tres epítetos seguidos: la fría lluvia, el oscuro bar, la triste barra. Con uno basta.
lines.meaning: Three epithets in a row: the cold rain, the dark bar, the sad counter. One is enough.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me quedo con la fría lluvia. Los otros dos eran puro adorno.
lines.meaning: I'll keep the cold rain. The other two were pure decoration.

bites.title: Paint, then tell
bites.rule: The imperfect paints the scene (llovía, olía, nadie hablaba); the preterite moves the plot (entró, pidió, se fue). A page of fiction needs both.
bites.example_meaning: It was raining when the stranger came in.

bites.title: Narrative imperfect
bites.rule: In novels and the press, an imperfect can tell one finished event in slow motion, often at the end: Dos días después, el alcalde dimitía.
bites.example: Al año siguiente, la fábrica cerraba sus puertas.
bites.example_meaning: The following year, the factory closed its doors.

bites.title: Inside a character's head
bites.rule: Free indirect style: third person and past tenses, but the questions and words are the character's: ¿Y si tenía razón? No, imposible.
bites.example: Miró el reloj. ¿Dónde se había metido Julia?
bites.example_meaning: He looked at his watch. Where on earth had Julia got to?

bites.title: Epithets
bites.rule: An adjective before the noun can stress a quality it already has: la blanca nieve, el frío mármol. It adds tone, not information.
bites.example: Apoyó la mano en el frío mármol.
bites.example_meaning: She rested her hand on the cold marble.

sorts.title: Scene or event?
sorts.why: The imperfect describes the setting of the story; the preterite marks the things that happen in it.

sorts.title: Which kind of literary word?
sorts.why: Penumbra and crepúsculo set the light; anhelo and inefable name feelings; susurrar and vislumbrar are things characters do.

spots.sentence: Cuando entró, el bar olió a café quemado.
spots.why: The smell is part of the scene, not an event: imperfect.

spots.sentence: Se detuvo en el umbrío de la puerta.
spots.why: El umbral is the threshold; umbrío means shady.

spots.sentence: En la penumbra se vislumbraba dos sombras.
spots.why: With se, the verb agrees with dos sombras: se vislumbraban.
The adjective agrees with alegría, which is feminine.

spots.sentence: En el cementerio yace sus abuelos.
spots.why: The subject is sus abuelos, plural: yacen.

builds.text: Llovía sobre el pueblo desde el amanecer.
builds.meaning: It had been raining on the village since dawn.

builds.text: Alguien susurraba en la penumbra del pasillo.
builds.meaning: Someone was whispering in the half-light of the corridor.

builds.text: Se detuvo en el umbral sin entrar.
builds.meaning: He stopped in the doorway without going in.
